note: Polarity control for fixtureguardctl. The two `history/` files are the pre-fix text of F004's and F005's guards, extracted verbatim from git; the two `fixed/` files are the landed fixes and are byte-identical to the live tree at the time this gate was added. `expect` declares the EXACT findings each fixture must produce as `line|shape|counter|bound|waived`, sorted — not a count, and not a boolean, so that deleting any one shape from the detector shows up here rather than being masked by another shape still firing. This manifest is read by `go run ./cmd/fixtureguardctl` on every gates run, not only by `go test`. `synthetic/production_budget_roles.rs` is shape C's control: it pins BOTH roles of a fixture-supplied production budget, so deleting either the rule or its two-role discriminator shows up here.

cases.why: F004: `assert!(refusals_before_the_drop < 4096, "the producer must never spin unboundedly before the drop lands")` inside the producer's `loop`, at line 280. Failed 2 runs in 5 on a loaded host with ws-core byte-identical to mainline.

F005: three owner loops guarded by `polls < POLL_BUDGET` with POLL_BUDGET = 2_000_000, at lines 69, 157 and 182. Failed `test-release` with `left: 179 right: 200` under other agents' load, with no defect anywhere. F005 records that two SIBLING loops carried the same guard, so all three are declared here.

The landed fix: a 30 s wall-clock deadline decides, and `refusals_before_the_drop` survives only inside the assertion MESSAGE. If the detector fired here it would be demanding the removal of a correct fix, which is how a gate gets routed around.

The landed fix: POLL_DEADLINE = 60 s decides in all three loops, `polls` only reports, and `disposed < 20` / `drained_idle_passes < 3` remain as GOAL conjuncts beside the deadline. Those two goals are the sharpest negative control the tree has: they are the same SHAPE as the guard that was removed, and only the increment separates them.

cases.provenance: hand-written from shapes present in rust/ws-core/tests and rust/ws-driver/tests
cases.why: Legitimate bounded-domain constants: a config value that is a count, a `for` over exactly 247 cases, a `while` bounded by `bytes.len()`, goal counters incremented conditionally beside a wall clock, an assertion about the system under test placed after the loop, and prose that quotes the defect.

cases.provenance: hand-written; covers the shapes history does not supply
cases.why: Shape B2 (a silent `if polls >= POLL_BUDGET { break }`), shape B1 via `panic!` rather than `assert!`, shape A on an atomic counter, one properly justified waiver that must be COUNTED rather than reported, and an unjustified waiver marker that must not silence the gate.

cases.provenance: hand-written; every shape in it is one rust/ws-testee/tests/loopback.rs actually carried before claude/adapter-residuals
cases.why: SHAPE C and the two roles `max_polls` serves. Firing: a count racing a 300ms wall-clock stall limit, the same through a forwarder, and the same through a forwarder whose parameter was RENAMED (which is why the rule keys on the assignment, not the name). Silent: a supply from a test that asserts BudgetExhausted, because reaching the bound is that test's asserted result rather than a slow host; a budget DERIVED from a stated duration, which is the remedy; and prose quoting the defect. Plus one justified waiver that must be counted and one unjustified marker that must not silence anything.
